items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A latent law \(P\) is a probability measure on \([-1,1]\times\{0,1\}^2\times\mathbb R\) with coordinates \((X,Y^0,Y^1,\varepsilon)\), admitting a continuous score density \(f(P,\cdot)\) on \([-1,1]\) and continuous versions \(\mu_d(P,\cdot)=\mathbb E_P[Y^d\mid X=\cdot]\), \(d\in\{0,1\}\), on the whole latent interval. For a public smoothness \(\beta\in(0,1]\) and a known noise scale \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), the observed triple is \(O=(W,D,Y)\) with \(W=X+\sigma\varepsilon\), \(D=\mathbf 1\{X\ge0\}\), \(Y=DY^1+(1-D)Y^0\), and \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is its law. The causal target is \(\theta(P)=\mu_1(P,0)-\mu_0(P,0)\), the H\"older seminorm is \([v]_\beta=\sup_{x\ne t}|v(x)-v(t)|/|x-t|^\beta\), \(s_1=1,\ s_0=-1\), \(\varphi_\sigma\) is the centered Gaussian density with standard deviation \(\sigma>0\), and \(\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\) is the benchmark law class.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: For an integer \(n\ge2\), the sample \(S_n=(O_i)_{i=1}^n\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\) is augmented by an independent seed \(U\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\), giving the experiment \(\mathbb P_{P,n}=P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\otimes\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\). \(\mathcal T_n\) is the class of all measurable maps \((S_n,U)\mapsto\mathbb R\), \(\mathcal I_{\beta,n,\sigma}\) the class of measurable connected closed subintervals of \([-1,1]\) with coverage at least \(0.9\) at every member of \(\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\), \(R_\beta(n,\sigma)\) the minimax absolute risk and \(\mathcal L_\beta(n,\sigma)\) the minimax worst expected length. For probability measures \(A,B\), \(\chi^2(A,B)=\int(dA/dB-1)^2\,dB\in[0,\infty]\) when \(A\ll B\) and \(\chi^2(A,B)=\infty\) otherwise, and \(\operatorname{TV}(A,B)=\sup_F|A(F)-B(F)|\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The public polynomial procedure: for an integer \(L\ge1\), \(T_L\) is the Chebyshev polynomial with \(T_L(\cos t)=\cos(Lt)\), \(K_L\) the positive endpoint kernel of degree \(m_L=3(L-1)\), \(Q_{L,\sigma}\) its finite inverse-heat transform, \(M_{L,\beta}=\int_0^1x^\beta K_L(x)\,dx\), \(V_L(\sigma)=\tfrac34\sum_{j=0}^{m_L}\sigma^{2j}(j!)^{-1}\int_0^1[K_L^{(j)}]^2\). The marked and unmarked averages \(\widehat A_{d,L},\widehat B_{d,L}\) have means \(A_{d,L}(P),B_{d,L}(P)\); \(\widehat\mu_{d,L}\) is the clipped ratio, \(\widehat\theta_L\) the effect estimate, \(\rho_L\) the public radius and \(I_L\) the interval, with fallback \(\widehat\theta_0=0\), \(\rho_0=1/2\), \(I_0=[-1/2,1/2]\). \(L_{\max}=\lceil n^{1/(4\beta+2)}\rceil\), \(L_\star\) is the smallest minimizer of \(\rho_L\) over \(\{0,\ldots,L_{\max}\}\), \(E_\beta(n,\sigma)=\rho_{L_\star}\), and \(\widetilde\theta_{\beta,n,\sigma}=\widehat\theta_{L_\star}\), \(\widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma}=I_{L_\star}\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: The lower-bound witnesses: for integers \(m\ge2\) and \(b,h\in(0,1]\), \(P_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}\) is the Legendre polynomial with \(P_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(1)=1\), \(N_m=(2m+1)^2-m^2\), \(g_m(t)=(1-t)N_m^{-1}\sum_{j=m}^{2m}(2j+1)(-1)^jP_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(2t-1)\), \(v_{b,m}\) its full-interval extension, \(\kappa=1/100\), \(P^\pm_{b,m}\) the Bernoulli-marked latent witnesses, \(q_\sigma(w)=\int_0^1\varphi_\sigma(w-x)dx\), \(u_{b,m,\sigma}(w)=\int_0^bg_m(x/b)\varphi_\sigma(w-x)dx\), \(\lambda_{b,\sigma}=b^2/(4\sigma^2)\), \(b_m(\sigma)=\min\{1,\sigma\sqrt m/8\}\), \(h_m(\sigma)=b_m(\sigma)/m^2\), the direct bump \(v_h^{\mathrm{dir}}\) and the direct witnesses \(P_h^{\mathrm{dir},\pm}\).

items.label: Setup S-5
items.nl:
The explicit rate: with \(
u=2 eta+1\) and \(h_0=n^{-1/
u}\), the noise cost \(\Psi(h,\sigma)\) on \((0,1]	imes[0,1]\) is \(0\) for \(\sigma\le h\), \((\sigma/h)^{2/3}-1\) for \(\sigma^4\le h<\sigma\), and \(h^{-1/2}\{1+\log(\sigma^2/\sqrt h)\}-1\) for \(h<\sigma^4\); \(h_\star(n,\sigma)\in[h_0,1]\) is the root of \(\log n+
u\log h=\Psi(h,\sigma)\), and \(r_ eta(n,\sigma)=h_\star(n,\sigma)^ eta\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl:
The exact latent-law class is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)=\{P:\;&\varepsilon\sim N(0,1),\quad
\varepsilon\perp(X,Y^0,Y^1),\\
&f(P,\cdot)\text{ is continuous on }[-1,1],\quad
\int_{-1}^{1}f(P,x)\,dx=1,\quad
\tfrac14\le f(P,x)\le\tfrac34\quad(x\in[-1,1]),\\
&\tfrac14\le\mu_d(P,x)\le\tfrac34
\quad(d\in\{0,1\},\ x\in[-1,1]),\\
&[\mu_d(P,\cdot)]_\beta\le2\quad(d\in\{0,1\})\}.
\end{split}
\]
The ambient law \(P\) has latent support \([-1,1]\times\{0,1\}^{2}\times\mathbb R\), as declared in the symbol catalog. The continuous score density has no imposed H\"older modulus. The full-domain potential-mean H\"older restriction is retained. Membership is a property of a single latent law. The observed score is \(W=X+\sigma\varepsilon\), and the sample for each integer \(n\ge2\) is \(S_n\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathcal I_{\beta,n,\sigma}=\{I:(S_n,U)\mapsto[\ell,\upsilon]\subset[-1,1],\ \ell\le\upsilon,\ I\text{ measurable},\ \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)}\mathbb P_{P,n}\{\theta(P)\in I\}\ge0.9\}\). The endpoints \(\ell,\upsilon\) are locally bound outputs.

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: \(K_L(x)=\bigl([1-T_L(1-2x)]/(2x)\bigr)^3\big/\int_0^1\bigl([1-T_L(1-2t)]/(2t)\bigr)^3\,dt\), with removable values filled continuously and polynomial extension to all real arguments.

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: \(\widehat A_{d,L}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{D_i=d\}Y_i Q_{L,\sigma}(s_dW_i),\quad \widehat B_{d,L}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{D_i=d\}Q_{L,\sigma}(s_dW_i),\quad \widehat\mu_{d,L}=\Pi_{[1/4,3/4]}\{\widehat A_{d,L}/\max(\widehat B_{d,L},1/8)\}\). Here \(\Pi\) denotes ordinary projection onto the displayed interval.

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: \(L_\star=\min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{L\in\{0,\ldots,L_{\max}\}}\rho_L,\quad E_\beta(n,\sigma)=\rho_{L_\star},\quad(\widehat\theta_{L_\star},I_{L_\star})\). The index zero uses the specified constant estimate and full target-range interval. All comparisons are deterministic functions of \((\beta,n,\sigma)\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: \(P^{\pm}_{b,m}: X\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[-1,1],\ Y^0\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\ Y^1\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\{1/2\pm\kappa(b/m^2)^\beta v_{b,m}(x)\}\), with conditionally independent potential outcomes and independent \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,1)\). The observed law is obtained by the same \((W,D,Y)\) map as for every member of \(\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\).

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl: \(P_h^{\mathrm{dir},\pm}: X\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[-1,1],\ \mu_0(P_h^{\mathrm{dir},\pm},x)=1/2,\ \mu_1(P_h^{\mathrm{dir},\pm},x)=1/2\pm\kappa h^\beta v_h^{\mathrm{dir}}(x)\), with conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes and independent standard Gaussian error.

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl: The endpoint precision handle comprises the causal target \(\theta\), the exact covariance \(V_L(\sigma)\), the public finite-sample certificate \(E_\beta(n,\sigma)\), and the legal witnesses \(P^\pm_{b_m(\sigma),m}\) and \(P_h^{\mathrm{dir},\pm}\). The delivered resolution rate and observable procedures are \(r_\beta(n,\sigma)\), \(\widetilde\theta_{\beta,n,\sigma}\), and \(\widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma}\) from the uniform-rate definition. The uniform-frontier theorem proves the two-sided minimax-risk and honest-length comparison to this rate for every \(n\ge2\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), including the degree cap, integer choices, both interfaces, and zero noise. The certificate is an upper guarantee whose comparability to the minimax quantities is proved; it does not define either minimax quantity.

items.label: Definition P-12
items.nl:
Put \(\nu=2\beta+1\) and \(h_0=n^{-1/\nu}\). For \(0<h\le1\) define
\[
\Psi(h,\sigma)=
\begin{cases}
0,&\sigma\le h,\\
(\sigma/h)^{2/3}-1,&\sigma^4\le h<\sigma,\\
h^{-1/2}\{1+\log(\sigma^2/\sqrt h)\}-1,&h<\sigma^4.
\end{cases}
\]
At \(\sigma=0\) only the first case applies. Define \(h_\star(n,\sigma)\) as the root in \([h_0,1]\) of
\[\log n+\nu\log h_\star(n,\sigma)=\Psi(h_\star(n,\sigma),\sigma),\]
and set
\[
r_\beta(n,\sigma)=h_\star(n,\sigma)^\beta,\qquad
\widetilde\theta_{\beta,n,\sigma}=\widehat\theta_{L_\star},\qquad
\widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma}=I_{L_\star}.
\]
The procedures use the finite public minimization in Definition 6; the root uses the displayed continuous increasing left side and continuous nonincreasing right side. Root existence and uniqueness, risk, and honesty are assertions proved below, rather than consequences assumed in this definition. The symbols \(\nu\) and \(h_0\) are local abbreviations. All tuning is procedure-side and adds no property to the law class.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: There is \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(L\ge1\), \(K_L\ge0\) on \([0,1]\), \(\int_0^1K_L(x)\,dx=1\), \(M_{L,\beta}\le C L^{-2\beta}\), and \(\int_0^1K_L(x)^2\,dx\le C L^2\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For every real polynomial \(p\) of degree at most \(m\) and every \(1\le j\le m\), \(\|p^{(j)}\|_{L^2[0,1]}\le 4^j(m+1)^{2j}\|p\|_{L^2[0,1]}/j!\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl: For every \(L\ge1\), \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), and \(x\in\mathbb R\), with an independent standard Gaussian \(\varepsilon\), \(\mathbb E Q_{L,\sigma}(x+\sigma\varepsilon)=K_L(x)\) and \(\mathbb E Q_{L,\sigma}(x+\sigma\varepsilon)^2=\sum_{j=0}^{m_L}\sigma^{2j}[K_L^{(j)}(x)]^2/j!\). Moreover, for an absolute \(C>0\), \(V_L(\sigma)\le C L^2\sum_{j=0}^{m_L}(C\sigma^2L^4)^j/(j!)^3\).

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl: For every \(m\ge2\) and \(b\in(0,1]\), \(g_m(0)=1\), \(g_m(1)=0\), \(\|g_m\|_\infty\le1\), \(\int_0^1g_m(t)^2\,dt\le1/N_m\), and \(\int_0^1t^kg_m(t)\,dt=0\) for \(0\le k\le m-2\). Also \(\|g_m^{(1)}\|_\infty\le7m^2\), \([v_{b,m}]_\beta\le7(b/m^2)^{-\beta}\), \(P^{\pm}_{b,m}\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\), and \(|\theta(P^+_{b,m})-\theta(P^-_{b,m})|=2\kappa(b/m^2)^\beta\).

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl: For \(\sigma>0\), every \(m\ge2\), and \(b\in(0,1]\), the full observed laws of \(P^+_{b,m}\) and \(P^-_{b,m}\) satisfy \[\chi^2((P^+_{b,m})_{\mathrm{obs}},(P^-_{b,m})_{\mathrm{obs}})\le16\kappa^2(b/m^2)^{2\beta}\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{u_{b,m,\sigma}(w)^2}{q_\sigma(w)}\,dw\le16\kappa^2(b/m^2)^{2\beta}\frac b{N_m}e^{b^2/(24\sigma^2)}\sum_{j=m-1}^{\infty}\frac{\lambda_{b,\sigma}^j}{j!}.\] The inequality includes both binary outcome cells and all real proxy values.

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl: For any \(b,m\) with \(\operatorname{TV}((P^+_{b,m})_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n},(P^-_{b,m})_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n})\le0.2\), \(R_\beta(n,\sigma)\ge0.8\kappa(b/m^2)^\beta\) and \(\mathcal L_\beta(n,\sigma)\ge1.2\kappa(b/m^2)^\beta\). The statements include arbitrary independent procedure randomization.

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
For \(R_j(t)=P_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(2t-1)\), \(j\ge1\),
\[
R_j'(t)=2\sum_{\substack{0\le k<j\\j-k\text{ odd}}}(2k+1)R_k(t),\qquad
\sup_{0\le t\le1}|R_j'(t)|\le j(j+1).
\]

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
The cost \(\Psi\) in \(\texttt{def:uniform-rate}\) is continuous, nonnegative, and nonincreasing in \(h\). For \(0<h\le t\le\sigma\le1\),
\[
(t/h)^{1/2}\le\frac{1+\Psi(h,\sigma)}{1+\Psi(t,\sigma)}\le t/h.
\]
For any locally bound \(a\ge1\) with \(ah\le1\),
\[1+\Psi(ah,\sigma)\le\max\{1,a^{-1/2}[1+\Psi(h,\sigma)]\}.\]

items.label: Lemma L-9
items.nl:
There is an absolute \(C>0\) such that for every integer \(L\ge1\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1]\),
\[V_L(\sigma)\le C L^2\exp\{C[1+\Psi(L^{-2},\sigma)]\}.\]

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\), every \(n\ge2\), \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), and \(L\ge1\), \(B_{d,L}(P)\ge1/4\), \(\mathbb E_{P,n}|\widehat\theta_L-\theta(P)|\le12M_{L,\beta}+28\sqrt{V_L(\sigma)/n}\), and \(\mathbb P_{P,n}\{\theta(P)\in I_L\}\ge0.9\). In particular \(I_{L_\star}\in\mathcal I_{\beta,n,\sigma}\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)}\mathbb E_{P,n}|\widehat\theta_{L_\star}-\theta(P)|\le E_\beta(n,\sigma)\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)}\mathbb E_{P,n}\operatorname{length}(I_{L_\star})\le2E_\beta(n,\sigma)\). These procedures are defined even when an arm is empty.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: There are \(c,C>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), \(R_\beta(n,\sigma)\ge c n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) and \(\mathcal L_\beta(n,\sigma)\ge c n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\). At \(\sigma=0\), both are at most \(C n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), attained in order by \((\widehat\theta_{L_\star},I_{L_\star})\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
Use \(r_\beta\), \(h_\star\), \(\Psi\), and the observable procedures in \(\texttt{def:uniform-rate}\). The root defining \(h_\star\) exists uniquely. For each fixed \(\beta\in(0,1]\), there are \(c,C>0\), independent of \(n\ge2\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), such that simultaneously
\[
c r_\beta(n,\sigma)\le R_\beta(n,\sigma)
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)}\mathbb E_{P,n}
|\widetilde\theta_{\beta,n,\sigma}-\theta(P)|
\le E_\beta(n,\sigma)\le C r_\beta(n,\sigma),
\]
\[
c r_\beta(n,\sigma)\le\mathcal L_\beta(n,\sigma)
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)}\mathbb E_{P,n}
\operatorname{length}(\widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma})
\le2E_\beta(n,\sigma)\le C r_\beta(n,\sigma),
\qquad\widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma}\in\mathcal I_{\beta,n,\sigma}.
\]
Here and in the following formulas, \(\asymp\) means comparison by positive constants depending only on \(\beta\), unless an additional fixed exponent is explicitly indicated. Set the local abbreviations \(\nu=2\beta+1\) and \(h_0=n^{-1/\nu}\). The following branch formulas are exhaustive for every sample size:

If \(\sigma\le h_0\), then \(h_\star=h_0\) exactly, including zero noise. If \(\sigma>h_0\), then \(h_0<h_\star<\sigma\). Its intermediate branch occurs exactly when
\[\log(n\sigma^{4\nu})\le\sigma^{-2}-1.\]
On this branch the unique local scalar \(z\in(1,\sigma^{-2}]\) satisfies
\[z+\frac{3\nu}{2}\log z=1+\log(n\sigma^\nu),\qquad
h_\star=\sigma z^{-3/2}\asymp\frac{\sigma}{[1+\log(n\sigma^\nu)]^{3/2}}.\]
When this inequality is reversed, the compact branch has a unique local scalar \(\tau>\sigma^{-2}\) satisfying
\[2\nu\log\tau+\tau\{1+\log(\sigma^2\tau)\}=\log n+1,\qquad h_\star=\tau^{-2},\]
and, uniformly on this branch,
\[
\tau\asymp\frac{\log(en)}{\log(e+\sigma^2\log(en))},\qquad
r_\beta(n,\sigma)\asymp
\left\{\frac{\log(e+\sigma^2\log(en))}{\log(en)}\right\}^{2\beta}.
\]
At the intermediate--compact equality, \(h_\star=\sigma^4\); at the direct--noisy equality, \(h_\star=\sigma=h_0\). Both formulas agree at their interfaces.

For fixed \(0<a<1/(2\beta+1)\), taking \(\sigma=n^{-a}\) gives, as \(n\) tends to infinity,
\[r_\beta(n,n^{-a})\asymp n^{-a\beta}(\log n)^{-3\beta/2},\]
where the constants in this simplified sequence formula may additionally depend on \(a\); fixed \(a\ge1/(2\beta+1)\) is the exact direct branch. At any fixed \(\sigma>0\), the order as \(n\) tends to infinity is \([\log\log(en)/\log(en)]^{2\beta}\). The root and finite-branch formulas, rather than that fixed-noise shorthand, govern every shrinking-noise sequence. Specifically, for \(\beta=1\) and \(\sigma=n^{-1/6}\), the intermediate branch holds for every \(n\ge2\) and
\[
r_1(n,n^{-1/6})=h_\star(n,n^{-1/6})\asymp
\frac{n^{-1/6}}{[1+\tfrac12\log n]^{3/2}}.
\]
All minimax lower bounds range over all procedures in the stated decision classes, with arbitrary independent randomization. No degree restriction is imposed on competing procedures.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
For the normalized Legendre polynomials and all nonnegative integers \(j,k\),
\[
\int_{-1}^{1}P_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(t)P_k^{\mathrm{Leg}}(t)\,dt
=\frac{2\mathbf1\{j=k\}}{2j+1},\qquad
P_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(-t)=(-1)^jP_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(t),\qquad
|P_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(t)|\le1\quad(-1\le t\le1).
\]
In particular \(P_j^{\mathrm{Leg}}(-1)=(-1)^j\).

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
Let \(H_j\) denote the probabilists\textquotesingle{} Hermite polynomial, defined by the generating function
\[
\exp(zt-t^2/2)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}H_j(z)\frac{t^j}{j!}.
\]
For a locally bound standard Gaussian variable \(Z\),
\[\mathbb E[H_j(Z)H_k(Z)]=j!\mathbf1\{j=k\},\qquad H_0=1.\]

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl:
For \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), define a larger Gaussian observed-treatment class \(\mathcal G(\sigma)\) as follows. Its members \(Q\) are probability laws on \(\mathbb R\times\{0,1\}^2\times\mathbb R\), with locally named coordinates \((Z,V^0,V^1,E)\). The score \(Z\) has a Lebesgue density \(a\) continuous and strictly positive on some open neighborhood of zero. For each \(d\in\{0,1\}\), the conditional mean \(v_d(z)=\mathbb E_Q[V^d\mid Z=z]\) admits a continuous version on that neighborhood. The error satisfies \(E\sim N(0,1)\). Define \(A=\mathbf1\{Z\ge0\}\), \(B=AV^1+(1-A)V^0\), and \(R=Z+\sigma E\), and require \(E\perp(Z,B)\). The observed sample comprises \(n\) independent copies of \((R,A,B)\), with the same independent uniform procedure seed. The causal target on this class is \(\vartheta(Q)=v_1(0)-v_0(0)\). Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathcal G}(n,\sigma)\) be the infimum over all measurable, possibly randomized estimates of the supremum of expected absolute error for \(\vartheta\). Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(n,\sigma)\) be the infimum of worst expected length over all measurable, possibly randomized connected closed intervals in \([-1,1]\) with coverage at least \(0.9\) at every member of \(\mathcal G(\sigma)\).

Every benchmark law in \(\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\) embeds in \(\mathcal G(\sigma)\), preserving both its observed experiment and its target. For each fixed \(\beta\in(0,1]\), there is \(c>0\), independent of \(n\ge2\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), such that
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathcal G}(n,\sigma)\ge R_\beta(n,\sigma)\ge c r_\beta(n,\sigma),\qquad
\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}(n,\sigma)\ge\mathcal L_\beta(n,\sigma)\ge c r_\beta(n,\sigma).
\]
For \(\sigma>0\), every member of \(\mathcal G(\sigma)\) satisfies the locally defined binary-response forms of Pei--Shen Assumption 1Y (the Gaussian error is independent jointly of the latent score and observed outcome), Assumption 2C (the score density is strictly positive near zero), and Assumption 7 (the scaled error is centered Gaussian); only this class-to-assumptions implication is asserted, not an equivalence. The comparison with Dong Assumptions 8--9 is provenance-only: the class definition directly imposes the corresponding cutoff-density, local conditional-mean continuity, Gaussian-error, and independence conditions, and the theorem has no Dong predicate or Dong-derived premise. The case \(\sigma=0\) is the noiseless completion. The matched upper bounds and honest attainers of \(\texttt{thm:uniform-frontier}\) are established only on \(\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\). They are not asserted on \(\mathcal G(\sigma)\), nor on Dong's stronger inference class from Assumptions 11 and 13 and Theorem 6. Any claim of supersmooth causal endpoint priority remains conditional on a complete literature and proof-assumption comparison.

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl:
The uniform precision question has the following positive answer on the exact class \(\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)\). Use the explicit piecewise cost \(\Psi\) and the unique scalar root in \(\texttt{def:uniform-rate}\), and put
\[
 r_\beta(n,\sigma)=h_\star(n,\sigma)^\beta,
 \qquad
 \widetilde\theta_{\beta,n,\sigma}=\widehat\theta_{L_\star},
 \qquad
 \widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma}=I_{L_\star}.
\]
The sample maps and the finite public minimization are exactly Definitions 5--6. For every fixed \(\beta\in(0,1]\) there are \(c,C>0\), independent of \(n\ge2\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), such that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 c r_\beta(n,\sigma)
 &\le R_\beta(n,\sigma)
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)}\mathbb E_{P,n}
                 |\widetilde\theta_{\beta,n,\sigma}-\theta(P)|
 \le E_\beta(n,\sigma)\le C r_\beta(n,\sigma),\\
 c r_\beta(n,\sigma)
 &\le\mathcal L_\beta(n,\sigma)
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\beta(\sigma)}\mathbb E_{P,n}
                 \operatorname{length}(\widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma})
 \le2E_\beta(n,\sigma)\le C r_\beta(n,\sigma),\\
 &\widetilde I_{\beta,n,\sigma}\in\mathcal I_{\beta,n,\sigma}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Writing locally \(\nu=2\beta+1\), the direct branch has \(h_\star=n^{-1/\nu}\) when \(\sigma\le n^{-1/\nu}\). In the noisy case the intermediate branch is selected exactly by
\[
 \log(n\sigma^{4\nu})\le\sigma^{-2}-1,
\]
and its scalar equation is
\[
 z+\frac{3\nu}{2}\log z=1+\log(n\sigma^\nu),
 \qquad h_\star=\sigma z^{-3/2}.
\]
The reverse inequality selects the compact branch, with scalar equation
\[
 2\nu\log\tau+\tau\{1+\log(\sigma^2\tau)\}=\log n+1,
 \qquad h_\star=\tau^{-2}.
\]
The equations agree at \(h_\star=\sigma^4\), and the direct interface is \(h_\star=\sigma=n^{-1/\nu}\). Their uniform scalar comparisons, including all shrinking-noise sequences, are those proved in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-frontier}\). In particular, at \(\beta=1\) and \(\sigma=n^{-1/6}\) the intermediate branch holds for every \(n\ge2\) and
\[
 r_1(n,n^{-1/6})\asymp
 \frac{n^{-1/6}}{[1+\tfrac12\log n]^{3/2}}.
\]
All displayed comparisons range over the full declared estimator and honest connected-interval decision classes, including independent randomization. The observed side label is \(D=\mathbf1\{X\ge0\}\); replacing it by assignment using the sign of \(W\) changes the experiment.

items.label: Cited result lem:pei-shen-identification-hypotheses
items.nl: Pei and Shen's Assumption 1Y requires measurement error independent jointly of the latent score and the observed outcome. Assumption 2C requires a score density strictly positive throughout some open neighborhood of the cutoff. Assumption 7 specifies centered Gaussian measurement error. Proposition 4(b) states that, under Assumptions 1Y, 2C, and 7, the continuous-score sharp RD contrast is identified. In this frozen carrier, each cutoff-side conditional mean is an ordinary integrable conditional expectation on some open neighborhood of zero: the observed outcome is absolutely integrable after restricting the latent score to that neighborhood, a real-valued regression representative satisfies the conditional-expectation identity there, and that representative has finite one-sided limits. No global outcome-integrability or potential-mean-continuity condition is imposed.

items.label: Cited result lem:dong-identification-hypotheses
items.nl: Dong's Chapter 2 Assumptions 8--9 require a positive cutoff density, continuous potential-mean traces there, continuous latent score and measurement error, and error independent of the score and observed outcome. These are identification-level conditions.

items.label: Cited result lem:dong-supersmooth-inference-comparison
items.nl: Dong's Chapter 2 Theorem 6, under all of Assumptions 8, 9, 11, and 13, gives pointwise asymptotic normality for the observed-treatment deconvolution local-linear contrast estimator displayed in (2.3.3). The centering is its finite-sample bias E[hat theta_{d,e}] - theta and the normalization is its finite-sample variance Var[hat theta_{d,e}]; Theorem 5 displays their leading ordinary-smooth expansions, and Theorem 6 says its bias is the same quantity as in Theorem 5 while leaving the supersmooth variance without an explicit leading formula. Assumption 13(3) quantifies that there exists eta > 0 and uses the Section 2.8.1 leading summand P^+_{1,n,1} (and the analogous minus-arm summand) in its displayed limit. The frozen comparison claim here is exclusively the centered-Gaussian specialization: the known error law is centered Gaussian at fixed scale, so Assumption 13 is specialized to supersmooth exponent two and the corresponding logarithmic bandwidth. Assumption 11 includes twice continuously differentiable local density and one-sided regression, transform-integrability restrictions, and kernel conditions; here its finite one-sided first- and second-derivative condition means finite left and right limits at zero of the derivatives taken on the punctured interior, together with continuity of the regression at zero; Assumption 13 also includes Fourier-supported kernel restrictions and its displayed Lyapunov condition. This theorem asserts no finite-sample minimax absolute-risk bound, honest expected-length lower bound, all-procedure converse, or uniformity over shrinking noise and zero. No dominance between its inference class and the present benchmark is asserted.

items.label: Cited result lem:zhang-karunamuni-accessible-scope
items.nl: The verified Zhang--Karunamuni scope is boundary estimation of a density or its derivatives from an additive independent-error model with known error law. The abstract, introduction, and accessible Section 4 excerpt describe asymptotic mean squared error for ordinary-smooth and supersmooth errors. These are statistical density targets and a squared-error criterion, rather than the present causal contrast and honest interval-length criterion. The full statements of Theorems 4.1--4.2 remain inaccessible in the inspected material. No exact theorem-rate, class-dominance, or supersmooth endpoint priority claim is attributed to this comparison.
